```python
def test_words_string():
    # Empty string returns empty list
    assert words_string("") == []
    
    # Single word, no commas
    assert words_string("hello") == ["hello"]
    
    # Words separated by commas
    assert words_string("one,two,three") == ["one", "two", "three"]
    
    # Words separated by spaces
    assert words_string("one two three") == ["one", "two", "three"]
    
    # Mixed commas and spaces
    assert words_string("one, two, three") == ["one", "two", "three"]
    
    # Comma-space separated (classic example)
    assert words_string("Hi, my name is John") == ["Hi", "my", "name", "is", "John"]
    
    # Consecutive commas act as single separator
    assert words_string("a,,b") == ["a", "b"]
    
    # Leading and trailing commas
    assert words_string(",hello,world,") == ["hello", "world"]
    
    # Only commas yields empty list
    assert words_string(",,,") == []
    
    # Only spaces yields empty list
    assert words_string("   ") == []
    
    # Single character
    assert words_string("a") == ["a"]
    
    # Single comma
    assert words_string(",") == []
    
    # Numbers as words
    assert words_string("1,2,3") == ["1", "2", "3"]
    
    # Tab and newline separated
    assert words_string("one\ttwo\nthree") == ["one", "two", "three"]
    
    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_words_string()
```
